title: Protein Secondary Structure Visualization with Time Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that visualizes protein secondary structure elements (alpha-helices, beta-sheets, and random coils/loops) with a time-based animation control system.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark background (0x0a0a1a). Camera at position (0, 5, 25) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x334455, intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one warm (0xffeedd) from (10,15,10) intensity 0.8, one cool (0xaaccff) from (-10,5,-10) intensity 0.4.
- OrbitControls for camera interaction.

PROTEIN BACKBONE MODEL:
- Generate a synthetic protein backbone as a sequence of 80 residues. Each residue has a 3D position along a path.
- The backbone path should be a smooth curve. Use CatmullRomCurve3 with control points that create a folded protein-like shape.
- Assign secondary structure types to residue ranges:
  * Residues 0-11: alpha-helix (color 0xff4466)
  * Residues 12-19: coil/loop (color 0xcccccc)
  * Residues 20-33: beta-sheet (color 0x44aaff)
  * Residues 34-41: coil/loop (color 0xcccccc)
  * Residues 42-55: alpha-helix (color 0xff4466)
  * Residues 56-63: coil/loop (color 0xcccccc)
  * Residues 64-79: beta-sheet (color 0x44aaff)

GEOMETRY REPRESENTATION:
- Alpha-helices: rendered as ribbon helices using TubeGeometry along a helical sub-path with radius 0.6. Use MeshPhongMaterial with shininess 80.
- Beta-sheets: rendered as flat arrow-shaped ribbons using ExtrudeGeometry or custom BufferGeometry, width 1.5, thickness 0.2. Use MeshPhongMaterial with shininess 60.
- Coils/loops: rendered as thin tubes (TubeGeometry, radius 0.15) with MeshPhongMaterial.
- All geometry segments are grouped under a single THREE.Group called proteinGroup.

TIME CONTROL / FOLDING ANIMATION:
- Implement a folding animation that morphs the protein from an extended (unfolded) linear chain to the final folded 3D structure.
- The animation progress is controlled by a normalized time parameter t in [0, 1]. At t=0 the chain is fully extended along the X-axis. At t=1 it is fully folded.
- Each residue position is interpolated: pos(t) = lerp(extendedPos, foldedPos, easedT) where easedT uses smoothstep easing.
- The animation rebuilds geometry each frame when t changes.

TIME CONTROL UI:
- A horizontal slider (range input) at the bottom center of the screen, width 400px, labeled 'Folding Progress'. Value range 0-100 mapping to t in [0,1].
- A 'Play/Pause' button that auto-advances t from current value to 1.0 at a rate of 0.15 per second. Toggles label between 'Play' and 'Pause'.
- A 'Reset' button that sets t back to 0 and stops playback.
- A speed selector dropdown with options: '0.5x', '1x', '2x', '4x' controlling the playback speed multiplier.
- A display showing current t value to 3 decimal places.

VISUALIZATION MODES:
- Three toggle buttons: 'Backbone', 'Ribbon', 'Cartoon'. Default is 'Ribbon'.
- Backbone mode: all segments rendered as thin tubes (radius 0.1).
- Ribbon mode: helices and sheets use their styled geometry (default).
- Cartoon mode: helices get larger radius (0.9), sheets get width 2.0, coils stay thin.
- Switching mode rebuilds geometry at current t value.

RESIDUE SELECTION:
- Clicking on the protein (raycasting) selects the nearest residue. Selected residue is highlighted with an emissive glow (emissive color 0xffff00, emissive intensity 0.5).
- A HUD panel (top-right, 200x120px, semi-transparent dark background) shows: residue index, secondary structure type, 3D position (x,y,z rounded to 2 decimals).

STATE MANAGEMENT - window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
- foldingProgress: current t value (number 0-1)
- isPlaying: boolean
- playbackSpeed: number (0.5, 1, 2, or 4)
- visualizationMode: string ('backbone'|'ribbon'|'cartoon')
- totalResidues: 80
- secondaryStructureCounts: { helix: 26, sheet: 30, coil: 24 }
- selectedResidue: number or null (index of selected residue)
- selectedResidueType: string or null ('helix'|'sheet'|'coil')
- residuePositions: array of {x,y,z} for all 80 residues at current t
- proteinCenter: {x,y,z} center of mass of all residue positions
- boundingBoxSize: {x,y,z} dimensions of protein bounding box
- geometryVertexCount: total vertex count of protein group
- animationFrameCount: number of frames rendered since page load

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Residue positions must interpolate smoothly between extended and folded conformations using smoothstep easing. At t=0 all residues must be collinear along X-axis. At t=1 the protein must occupy a compact 3D volume. The center of mass must shift continuously. Bounding box X dimension must decrease monotonically as t increases from 0 to 1. No NaN values in any position. All 80 residue positions must be finite numbers at all times.
